standardsBasis: Texas TEKS (2012 text, 19 TAC Ch. 111) primary; Common Core (CCSS) cross-reference

fieldDocs.skills[]: id, order (1-based within grade, = recommended teaching order), name, teks[{code,verified}], ccss[] (trailing ? = unconfirmed), description, season[], generator, examples[3], mastery, levels[], keypad[]

fieldDocs.levels[]: id (skillId.Ln), order (difficulty ascending), name, params (partial overrides of generator.operands/flags; absent key = inherit)

gradeMapping.principle: Grade is a recommended starting band, not a gate. A child picks (or a parent sets) a grade; inside it, skills unlock in `order`. Children can jump to any grade.
levelModel: Level = one skill's sub-level (skillId.Ln). Do not reuse the current integer User.level for this; keep it as the XP/star level and add per-skill progress.
Unlock next skill when previous skill mastery (accuracyPct, secondsPerProblem) is met on the last 20 problems; allow parent override.
Interleave 20% review from earlier skills and grades (spaced repetition) in Practice/Testing.
Mode mapping: Memorize = show answer first then recall (levels with new facts); Practice = untimed or soft-timed with feedback; Testing = timed at secondsPerProblem; Spelling Bee unchanged.

timesTablesPlacement.grade3: Core: 100 of 144 existing Problem rows (both factors 1-10) plus x0 facts; recommended order x2,x10,x5,x0/1, x4,x3, x9 and squares, x6/x7/x8; division facts follow each set.
timesTablesPlacement.grade4: Remaining 44 rows (a factor of 11 or 12) and squares to 15x15.
timesTablesPlacement.grades5and6: Review only, resurfaced through spaced repetition and as sub-skills of other problems.

localDbObservations: Problem: 144 rows (id, problem text like '1 x 1' with lowercase x, answer integer, correct, incorrect, mastered). UserProblem(userId, problemId, everCorrect, updatedAt, mastered) composite PK. User.level integer default 1. 413 UserProblem rows locally.
Answer is an integer column: cannot store fractions, decimals, remainders or symbols.
Per-user mastery already exists for the 144 table rows; new skills are generated on the fly, so mastery must be keyed by (userId, skillId, level) and, for fact skills, optionally (a,b) pairs.
gradeMapping.schemaSuggestion: Add Skill progress table (userId, skillId, levelOrder, attempts, correct, recentWindow json, masteredAt) and store answers as text with answerType; keep Problem/UserProblem untouched for tables and map grade 3/4 skills to them via a (a,b) key. Generated items do not need rows.

keypadNeeds.notes: Exists today. Raise max entry length to 7 digits (grade 4 add/sub to 1,000,000) and keep manual Enter for multi-digit answers (no auto-submit); auto-submit is fine for facts.
Comparison skills; replace keypad by 3 big buttons.
Money in grade 3; decimals grade 4+. Accept '.5', '0.50', '3', '3.0'. Compare numerically, not as strings.
Accept 'a/b' and 'w a/b'. Mark right if equal value unless the prompt says 'simplest form'. Show a stacked-fraction preview.
Two fields (quotient, remainder) preferred to typing 'R'; label the second field 'R'. Remainder-free levels show one field.
Unary minus only at start; display with a true minus sign; allow toggle +/-.
Fraction, exponent (superscript), absolute value bars, thousand separators in prompts; coin images for money skills; use proper minus and multiplication signs but accept 'x' in stored text.
secondsPerProblem includes entry time; add ~1 s for 3-digit answers, ~2 s for 5-digit in thresholds only if real play data shows kids missing them; otherwise keep as listed.

researchNotes: Accuracy target: 90% for computation skills, 95% for fact-recall skills (counting, facts, comparisons). Chosen as a design default; TEKS/CCSS give no numeric thresholds.

Speed: about 3 s per recalled single-digit fact (retrieval) is the widely used 'automatic' criterion; this includes typing a 1-2 digit answer, so 3 s is a strict but standard target. Multi-step procedures get longer budgets scaled to the number of digit operations.

Strategy order for addition/subtraction: counting/+0/+1, doubles, make-ten (+9, +8), near doubles, then the rest; subtraction follows as the inverse (Baroody-style reasoning-strategy framework; seen via secondary sources).

Strategy order for multiplication: x2, x10, x5 first (skip counting; the NCTM-linked Georgia document places 2s/5s/10s first), then x0/x1, x4 (double double), x3, x9, squares, finally x6/x7/x8 (6x7, 6x8, 7x8 are the hardest). Division facts are taught right after the matching multiplication set.

A 2015 study cited in search results found a strategy-based approach produced steadier multiplication-fact gains than repetition drills alone: combine Memorize (strategy shown) with Practice/Testing (retrieval).

grades.label: 1st grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: In the 2012 TEKS text read for this spec, 1.3D is the within-20 fact-strategy SE (make 10, decompose to 10). 1.3F is 'create and solve problem situations from a number sentence', not a fluency SE. CCSS 1.OA.C.6 is the true fluency target (add/subtract within 10 fluently, within 20 with strategies).
grades.timesTables: None. Skip-counting by 2, 5, 10 (1.5B) is the on-ramp to x2, x5, x10.

skills.name: Count forward and back (to 120)
skills.description: Say what comes before/after a number and fill a missing number in a counting sequence up to 120.

constraints: Missing term is first, middle or last of a 3-term run

skills.name: Skip count by 2s, 5s, 10s
skills.description: Give the next number when counting by 2, 5 or 10 (up to 120). Foundation for x2/x5/x10 facts.

constraints: start is a multiple of step

skills.name: 10 more / 10 less
skills.description: Mentally find the number 10 more or 10 less than a number up to 120.

skills.name: Tens and ones
skills.description: Read a number as tens and ones and write the number (to 99, then 120).

constraints: Prompt forms: 'T tens O ones', 'T0 + O', 'how many tens in N'

skills.name: Compare two-digit numbers
skills.description: Choose <, > or = for two numbers up to 100.

constraints: Level 1 tens digits differ; level 2 same tens digit

skills.name: Addition facts within 10
skills.description: Recall sums with total <= 10. Ordered by strategy: +0/+1, doubles, sums to 5, make 10.

mastery.note: Target ~3 s recall (Baroody-style convention; see sources).

skills.name: Subtraction facts within 10
skills.description: Recall differences from totals <= 10, linked to addition partners.

skills.name: Addition facts within 20
skills.description: Recall sums 11-20 using make-ten, doubles and near-doubles strategies.

constraints: Order of levels follows strategy: doubles, +9/make-ten, near doubles, rest

skills.name: Subtraction facts within 20
skills.description: Subtract within 20 by counting back to 10 or thinking of the missing addend.

constraints: Level 1 is the inverse of doubles

skills.name: Find the missing number
skills.description: Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation within 20.

constraints: Unknown can be any position (a+_=c, _+b=c, c-_=a, _-b=a)

levels.name: within 10, unknown is a term after the +

skills.name: Add and subtract tens
skills.description: Add/subtract multiples of 10 and add a one-digit number to a two-digit number with no regrouping.

constraints: Level 3: two-digit + one-digit, ones sum <= 9 (no regrouping)

skills.name: Count coins (pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters)
skills.description: Total value in cents of a small set of coins. (CCSS puts coins in grade 2; Texas starts them in grade 1.)

constraints: Level 1 coins of one kind or dimes+pennies

mastery.note: Prompt uses coin pictures or words; answer is cents.

outOfScope.adaptation: 'Half of 8' / 'Fourth of 12' as integer answers once skip counting is mastered.

outOfScope.topic: Data displays, measurement with units, time to the hour/half-hour, 2D/3D shape attributes
outOfScope.adaptation: Out of scope. 'How many minutes in a half hour' style recall (30) is the only drillable bit.
Short story problems could reuse g1-add/sub generators with a text template; needs reading support.

grades.label: 2nd grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: TEKS 2.4A: quickly recall addition and subtraction facts within 20 (2012 text). TEKS 2.4B: add up to four 2-digit numbers and subtract 2-digit numbers mentally/with place value. CCSS 2.OA.B.2 and 2.NBT.B.5 are the fluency standards.
grades.timesTables: Foundation only: equal groups and arrays to 5x5 (CCSS 2.OA.C.4); skip counting by 2, 5, 10, 100. Several US programs introduce x2/x5/x10 in late grade 2 (NCTM-linked Georgia doc, see sources).

skills.name: Addition facts within 20 (automatic)
skills.description: Know all sums of two one-digit numbers from memory.

constraints: Includes all pairs 0-10 + 0-10, weighted toward sums 11-18

skills.name: Subtraction facts within 20 (automatic)
skills.description: Know all differences from totals up to 18 from memory (inverse of addition facts).

skills.name: Hundreds, tens, ones
skills.description: Read, write and decompose numbers to 1,000 (Texas goes to 1,200).

constraints: Include zeros in tens/ones places in later levels

examples.prompt: Digit in the tens place of 583?

skills.name: Compare numbers to 1,000
skills.description: Choose <, > or = for two 3-digit numbers.

constraints: Levels: hundreds differ, then tens differ, then ones differ

skills.name: Skip count by 5s, 10s, 100s
skills.description: Next term in a skip-counting sequence; bridge to multiplication.

skills.name: Add two-digit numbers
skills.description: Mental/written addition of 2-digit numbers; up to four addends.

skills.name: Subtract two-digit numbers
skills.description: Subtract 2-digit from 2-digit; regrouping introduced after no-regroup mastery.

skills.name: Mentally 10 or 100 more/less
skills.description: Add or subtract 10 or 100 from a 3-digit number without writing.

skills.name: Add within 1,000
skills.description: 3-digit addition using place value, with regrouping introduced gradually.

skills.name: Subtract within 1,000
skills.description: 3-digit subtraction using place value; regrouping introduced gradually.

skills.name: Coin totals to $1
skills.description: Total cents for up to ~6 mixed coins.

skills.name: Equal groups and arrays (x intro)
skills.description: Repeated addition and rows x columns up to 5 x 5; first contact with x2, x5, x10.

constraints: Show as 'n groups of k', 'k + k + k', or an array picture

levels.name: groups of 3 and 4, up to 5 groups

outOfScope.topic: Rounding (not in 2012 TEKS grade 2 per text read); data/graphs; measurement; 2D/3D geometry; telling time to 5 min
outOfScope.adaptation: Time: 'minutes after the hour' from a clock image could be drilled; needs images.
'How many fourths make a whole?' (4) as integer; 'half of 16' (8).

grades.label: 3rd grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: TEKS 3.4F: recall facts to multiply up to 10 by 10 with automaticity and recall the corresponding division facts. 3.4A: fluently add/subtract within 1,000. CCSS 3.OA.C.7 (multiply/divide within 100, know single-digit products from memory by end of grade) and 3.NBT.A.2 (add/subtract within 1,000).
grades.timesTables: CORE GRADE FOR THE EXISTING TABLES. Rows of the Problem table where both factors are 1-10 (100 of 144 rows) are grade 3. Add x0 (not in the table) and division facts. Rows with a factor of 11 or 12 (44 rows) are grade 4 enrichment.

skills.name: Round to nearest 10 or 100
skills.description: Round numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest 10 or 100.

constraints: Include midpoint values (x5 -> up, 50 -> 100 for hundreds)

skills.name: Add within 1,000 (fluent)
skills.description: Add 3-digit numbers fluently including regrouping.

skills.name: Subtract within 1,000 (fluent)
skills.description: Subtract 3-digit numbers fluently including borrowing across zeros.

skills.name: Multiplication: x0, x1, x2, x5, x10
skills.description: Easiest facts first: skip-count based and identity/zero facts. Commutative partners count as the same fact.

constraints: Present either order (a x b or b x a)
Matches rows of existing Problem table where a factor is 1, 2, 5 or 10

skills.name: Multiplication: x3, x4
skills.description: x4 as double-double; x3 as double plus one more group.

constraints: Interleave 20% review from earlier fact sets

skills.name: Multiplication: x9 and squares
skills.description: x9 via ten-minus-one pattern; square facts 6x6..10x10 as anchors.

constraints: Level 2 squares only: n x n for n 6-10

skills.name: Multiplication: x6, x7, x8
skills.description: Hardest facts last; only the unfamiliar ones remain (6x7, 6x8, 7x8 and mirrors).

constraints: Exclude pairs already covered by earlier levels (x2,x5,x10,x9,squares); remaining unique facts are 6x7, 6x8, 7x8 and x6/x7/x8 with 3 and 4

mastery.note: Spend most spaced repetition here; 6x7, 6x8, 7x8 are the usual last holdouts.

skills.name: Multiplication: full 10 x 10 (automatic)
skills.description: All 0-10 products, random order, timed. This is the existing app drill capped at 10.

skills.name: Division facts (inverse of x)
skills.description: Divide within 100 by a one-digit divisor with whole-number quotient; follows the same grouping as multiplication.

constraints: Introduce a division fact set only after its multiplication set is mastered

skills.name: Missing factor
skills.description: Find the unknown factor; links multiplication to division.

constraints: Unknown can be first or second factor

skills.name: One-digit x multiple of 10
skills.description: Multiply 1-9 by 10-90 using the base fact and place value.

skills.name: Two-digit x one-digit
skills.description: Texas teaches 2-digit x 1-digit in grade 3 (CCSS defers it to grade 4).

constraints: Level 1 no carrying (ones product <= 9 and tens product <= 9); Level 2 carry once; Level 3 carry twice

skills.name: Even or odd
skills.description: Decide parity of numbers to 1,000 using the ones digit.

skills.name: Equivalent fractions (denominators 2,3,4,6,8)
skills.description: Fill the missing numerator to make equal fractions.

constraints: den2 is a multiple of den1

skills.name: Compare fractions (same numerator or denominator)
skills.description: Choose <, >, = when the fractions share a numerator or denominator.

constraints: Same denominator OR same numerator, never both different

skills.name: Money totals with dollars
skills.description: Total of bills and coins, answered in dollars with a decimal point.

outOfScope.topic: Area/perimeter (3.6), elapsed time (3.7), measurement, graphs (3.8), 2D shapes (3.6)
outOfScope.adaptation: Area/perimeter of a rectangle with integer sides is drillable as a one-number answer; elapsed time as minutes.
Out of scope; could wrap generators in story templates.

grades.label: 4th grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: TEKS 4.4H: fluently solve one- and two-step multiplication and division problems, including interpreting remainders. 4.4A add/subtract whole numbers and decimals to hundredths with the standard algorithm; 4.4C includes perfect squares up to 15x15. CCSS 4.NBT.B.4 (fluent add/subtract with standard algorithm, to 1,000,000).
grades.timesTables: 11s, 12s and squares to 15x15 (4.4C) live here: the 44 Problem rows with a factor 11 or 12 map to the grade 4 level g4-mult-11-15; grade 3 rows are reviewed with spaced repetition rather than retaught.

skills.name: Place value and rounding to 1,000,000
skills.description: Round whole numbers to any place through hundred thousands; read digit values.

constraints: Include midpoint and 9-carry cases (e.g. 7,951 to nearest 100)

examples.prompt: Round 365,810 to the nearest hundred thousand

skills.name: Add/subtract multi-digit numbers
skills.description: Standard-algorithm addition/subtraction up to 6 digits.

skills.name: Multiply by 10 and 100
skills.description: Place-value shift: multiply a number by 10 or 100.

skills.name: Multiplication beyond 10: 11s, 12s, squares to 15x15
skills.description: Finishes the 12x12 table and the perfect squares through 15x15.

constraints: Rows of existing Problem table with a factor 11 or 12 (44 rows)

skills.name: Multiply 2-4 digit by 1-digit
skills.description: Standard algorithm or partial products for up to a four-digit number by a single digit.

skills.name: Multiply 2-digit x 2-digit
skills.description: Two-digit by two-digit multiplication.

skills.name: Divide by a one-digit number, with remainders
skills.description: Up to 4-digit dividend, divisor 2-9; answer as quotient and remainder.

skills.name: Estimate by rounding
skills.description: Estimate sums, differences, products by rounding to a stated place.

constraints: Prompt states the place to round to

skills.name: Factors and multiples
skills.description: Is X a factor of N? What is the next multiple of K? (No direct grade 4 SE in 2012 TEKS text read; related to 5.4A.)

skills.name: Equivalent fractions
skills.description: Fill missing numerator or denominator for an equal fraction.

skills.name: Compare fractions
skills.description: Compare using benchmarks (0, 1/2, 1) or common denominators.

constraints: Level 1 benchmark 1/2; level 2 unlike denominators with multiples; level 3 any

skills.name: Add/subtract fractions, same denominator
skills.description: Add and subtract like fractions; improper results allowed (mixed forms accepted).

skills.name: Tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals
skills.description: Convert tenths/hundredths between fraction and decimal; pick the greater decimal.

constraints: Comparison pairs differ by place-value trap (0.4 vs 0.35)

skills.name: Add/subtract decimals to hundredths (money)
skills.description: Standard algorithm for decimals to hundredths; money context.

constraints: Same decimal places first, then 1 vs 2 places

outOfScope.topic: Angles/measurement (4.7), 2D shape attributes (4.6), line plots and data (4.9), financial literacy
outOfScope.adaptation: 'Angle sum in a triangle', 'supplementary angle' as integer answers; protractor reading out of scope.
'Rule: add 6. 4, 10, 16, __' integer answers; fits existing skip-count generator.

grades.label: 5th grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: TEKS 5.3 contains the fluency SEs: 5.3B (3-digit x 2-digit standard algorithm), 5.3C (up to 4-digit by 2-digit divide), 5.3K (add/subtract positive rational numbers fluently). CCSS 5.NBT.B.5 is the fluency standard (multi-digit multiply with the standard algorithm); 5.NBT.B.6 and 5.NBT.B.7 cover division and decimal operations.
grades.timesTables: None new. The full 12x12 table is review; spaced repetition resurfaces unmastered facts inside multi-digit problems.

skills.name: Decimal place value and rounding
skills.description: Value of a digit and rounding decimals to tenths or hundredths.

skills.name: Multiply/divide by powers of 10
skills.description: Shift the decimal point; exponents of 10.

skills.name: Multiply 3-digit x 2-digit
skills.description: Standard algorithm; core fluency target for grade 5.

skills.name: Divide by a two-digit divisor
skills.description: Up to 4-digit dividend by 2-digit divisor; whole quotient first, then remainder.

constraints: Level 3 with remainder (CCSS also allows decimal quotient later)

skills.name: Add/subtract decimals
skills.description: Positive decimals to hundredths (thousandths for compare only), mixed place counts.

constraints: Subtraction non-negative; align-decimals traps with whole numbers (10 - 3.62)

skills.name: Multiply decimals
skills.description: Decimal x whole, then decimal x decimal to hundredths; money.

constraints: Product has <= 4 decimal places in level 3

skills.name: Divide decimals
skills.description: Quotients to hundredths with whole-number divisors (2-digit); terminating results only.

skills.name: Add/subtract fractions, unlike denominators
skills.description: Common denominators with small denominators; answers as fraction (improper OK) or mixed number.

constraints: Level 1: one denominator multiple of the other
Accept equivalent forms; ask simplest form only in last level

levels.name: one denominator is a multiple of the other

skills.name: Multiply fraction by whole number
skills.description: Whole x fraction (Texas stops there; fraction x fraction is grade 6).

constraints: Result may be integer, proper or improper

skills.name: Divide with unit fractions
skills.description: Unit fraction / whole, whole / unit fraction.

skills.name: Order of operations (grouping)
skills.description: Evaluate whole-number expressions with parentheses/brackets; no exponents (Texas).

skills.name: Prime or composite
skills.description: Classify numbers to 100 as prime or composite.

outOfScope.topic: Volume of prisms (5.6), coordinate plane graphing (5.8), data (5.9), measurement conversion
outOfScope.adaptation: Volume l x w x h as integer; ordered pair coordinates would need a grid widget.

grades.label: 6th grade
grades.texasFluencyNote: TEKS 6.3D: add, subtract, multiply and divide integers fluently. 6.3E: multiply and divide positive rational numbers fluently (the 2012 text marks both as fluency SEs). Texas puts integer operations in grade 6; CCSS places them in grade 7 (7.NS.A.1-2). CCSS 6.NS.B.2 (multi-digit division), 6.NS.B.3 (multi-digit decimal operations) are the CCSS grade 6 fluency standards.
grades.timesTables: None new. Spaced review of any unmastered fact seeded into integer/fraction/percent problems; GCF/LCM and exponents lean on 12x12 recall.

skills.name: Multiply fractions and mixed numbers
skills.description: Fraction x fraction, then mixed numbers; simplify.

skills.name: Divide fractions and mixed numbers
skills.description: Divide using the reciprocal.

constraints: Results are integers or simple fractions

skills.name: Multi-digit whole-number division
skills.description: Standard algorithm: 3-5 digit dividend by 2-digit divisor, whole quotients.

constraints: Whole quotient (no remainder) in L1; remainder or decimal after

skills.name: Decimal operations (+, -, x, /)
skills.description: All four operations with decimals to thousandths; divisors may be decimals.

skills.name: Opposites and absolute value
skills.description: Opposite and absolute value of integers to +/-100.

skills.name: Add/subtract integers
skills.description: Integers within +/-20 then +/-100; subtraction of negatives.

constraints: Show subtraction of a negative as '- (-n)'

skills.name: Multiply/divide integers
skills.description: Sign rules with facts to 12x12.

skills.name: Fraction / decimal / percent conversion
skills.description: Convert benchmark values among forms.

constraints: Percent answers are the number only (prompt shows %)

levels.name: fraction to percent (halves, fourths, fifths, tenths)

skills.name: Percent of a number (benchmarks)
skills.description: 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, then multiples; mental math.

constraints: Result is an integer or terminating decimal; n chosen to divide cleanly

skills.name: Equivalent ratios and unit rates
skills.description: Missing term in equivalent ratios; unit rate by division.

examples.prompt: 120 miles in 3 hours: miles per hour

skills.name: Exponents and order of operations
skills.description: Evaluate whole-number powers and expressions with exponents.

constraints: Level 1 squares/cubes; Level 3 mixed with +,x and parentheses

skills.name: GCF and LCM
skills.description: Greatest common factor and least common multiple of two numbers up to 100 (GCF) / 12 (LCM). TEKS location not confirmed in 2012 text read.

skills.name: One-step equations
skills.description: Solve x + p = q, p x = q, x / p = q with whole numbers.

levels.name: x + p = q / x - p = q

outOfScope.topic: Area of triangles/polygons (6.8), data displays, box plots, statistics (6.12), inequalities graphing
outOfScope.adaptation: Area of a right triangle (b x h / 2) with integer sides; mean/median of a short list as integer answer.
